title: Verifier‑Augmented vs. LLM‑Only NetOps Agents: A Paired Evaluation on an Action‑Aware Staging Benchmark
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline on a compact action‑aware staging benchmark (ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1). Two preregistered design choices—shared_initial_generation (one shared LLM candidate per task delivered to both conditions) and reuse of the same deterministic validator as both the runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer—produced a deterministic ceiling effect in this run that rendered the preregistered primary estimand (paired safe‑deploy difference) effectively untestable for generator×guard closed‑loop dynamics. The preregistered design (cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1) used gpt‑5‑mini as the generator, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as runtime guard and scorer, N=400 paired tasks (800 episodes) and shared_initial_generation semantics. Confirmatory outcomes (archived artifacts) show complete_pairs = 400; baseline_success_count = 400/400; guarded_success_count = 400/400; paired contingency n_11 = 400, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0; observed paired difference = 0.0; preregistered permutation p = 1.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). We present the preregistered methodology, the exact artifact‑grounded results, a diagnostic analysis explaining why the design choices produced a ceiling, and concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations to harden future benchmarks so they expose generator×guard interactions.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into network configuration artifacts and staged change workflows (canaries, progressive rollouts, rollback). Prior work shows LLMs can synthesize plausible configuration templates in controlled settings, and separate lines of research demonstrate that verifier‑guided generate–validate–repair loops and deterministic network verifiers reduce syntactic and semantic IaC errors. The operational question we address is end‑to‑end: under realistic staging semantics, how do generator variability, runtime verification, staged rollouts, repair, and rollback interact to affect safe‑deploy outcomes?

Research question. Under the registered benchmark semantics, does integrating a deterministic runtime validator with an LLM generator increase the paired safe‑deploy rate relative to an LLM‑only pipeline? The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in safe‑deploy rate (guarded − baseline) measured on N=400 paired tasks.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation (cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1) using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; (2) exact, archived confirmatory results showing a deterministic ceiling (both conditions accepted the shared candidates for all pairs); (3) a diagnosis grounded in the preserved validator traces explaining why the preregistered design removed signal for generator×guard interaction; and (4) concrete, artifact‑grounded benchmark‑hardening recommendations for future confirmatory studies.
sections.related_work: This work draws on four literatures. First, intent→configuration translation studies demonstrate that LLMs can generate usable configuration artifacts in benchmarks and testbeds (Nguyen et al., 2024; Li et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2025). Second, verifier‑guided generate–validate–repair workflows report correctness gains in IaC and provisioning contexts (Jana et al., 2026), motivating analogous integrations for NetOps. Third, deterministic network verification and reachability tools effectively find configuration errors in emulated/offline settings (Liu et al., 2025), though tool assumptions differ across network models. Fourth, agentic and tool‑augmented LLM architectures expand AIOps functionality but introduce new failure modes (hallucination, misapplied tools) that motivate runtime guardrails and staged deliveries (Pei et al., 2025; Rahman & Swapnil, 2026; Abbasli et al., 2026). Surveys repeatedly note an evaluation gap: standardized, action‑aware benchmarks combining generation, runtime blocking, staged rollouts, repair, rollback, and provenance are limited. Our experiment operationalizes a compact action‑aware staging benchmark under a strict preregistered design to probe verifier utility and to surface practical design pitfalls.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands. The study was preregistered (cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1). The primary confirmatory estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (two‑sided inference, α=0.05). The preregistered analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) implements a permutation‑based paired difference test and reports exact permutation p‑values; we also produced an exact McNemar two‑sided test for corroboration. Bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) were frozen for secondary outcomes.

Adapter semantics and shared generation. Execution used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with declared generator gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as both runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer. Critically, the preregistration set shared_initial_generation = true (independent_condition_generation = false): each task invoked a single deterministic LLM generation delivered identically to both the baseline and guarded episodes. This choice intentionally isolates the validator’s acceptance decision on identical generator outputs rather than exposing independent generator variance between conditions. Together these choices render the preregistered primary estimand effectively untestable in this execution, because the guard had no opportunity to intervene when the shared candidate was accepted.

Episode flow, repair policy, deterministic replay. For each task the adapter requested a single shared candidate from gpt‑5‑mini, delivered that candidate to both episodes, and (in the guarded episode) routed the candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which applied full intent‑constraint validation. The preregistered repair policy allowed up to one repair attempt in the guarded episode; repair invocations, repair_applied flags, validation_before/after states, and final validity decisions were recorded. Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and preregistered three‑replay consistency checks were applied; per the preregistration any nondeterministic or simulator‑error pairs would be excluded. All runtime and analysis code, seeds, and logs are archived in the execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run began 2026‑08‑29T18:23:37Z and completed 2026‑08‑29T19:12:38Z. Planned episodes = 800; completed episodes = 800; failed episodes = 0; model_calls_used = 400 (shared initial generation); complete_pairs = 400. Deterministic three‑replay checks passed for all pairs; no exclusions were recorded.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑grounded). Baseline_success_count = 400 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0); guarded_success_count = 400 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency: n_11 = 400; n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. The preregistered permutation test returned p = 1.0; the exact McNemar two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). These numbers are reproduced directly from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/*).

Repair and rollback. Across the 800 episodes repair_applied = false and no rollbacks were invoked; validator_trace entries show validation_after.final_state matched expected_final_state for accepted configurations, which explains universal acceptance of the shared candidates.

Difficulty composition (artifact provenance and limitation). The per‑task difficulty labels for all N=400 tasks are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. To avoid inventing aggregated totals that are not reproduced within this manuscript text, we report an explicit verified representative sample from the preserved manifest: among the first six representative tasks included in the archived manifest the difficulty labels are {medium (1), hard (2), very_hard (3)}. The full per‑task difficulty labels are archived and available for auditors to aggregate deterministically (execution/task_manifest.jsonl).
sections.discussion:
Why the primary estimand was uninformative. Two preregistered design choices produced the deterministic ceiling. First, shared_initial_generation removed generator variance by delivering identical LLM outputs to both episodes. Second, the runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer were the same deterministic implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). When the deterministic validator accepts the shared candidate, both conditions necessarily record identical safe‑deploy outcomes, so the paired difference must be zero. This is a construct‑validity outcome of the frozen design, not a general null statement about verifier utility across diverse generator/validator pairings.

Consequences for power and inference. The preregistered power calculation assumed within‑pair variability that did not occur; the observed ceiling therefore invalidates the original power rationale and collapses inferential variance. Exact p‑values of 1.0 correctly reflect the data but do not adjudicate whether a runtime guard would have improved outcomes under an alternative design that preserved generator variance.

Benchmark‑hardening recommendations (artifact‑grounded). Using archived validator_trace and execution accounting we recommend implementable steps for future preregistered runs that preserve signal for generator×guard interactions: (1) independent per‑condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true); (2) distinct runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer (or a held‑out scorer) to avoid conflation; (3) controlled adversarial seeding to ensure reproducible baseline failures; (4) difficulty‑stratified sampling using the archived task difficulty labels; (5) instrumented mitigation metrics (repair attempts, repairs applied, time‑to‑rollback) already present in validator_trace entries. These steps can be applied directly using the archived manifests and validator traces.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline. Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator pairing, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and both conditions produced 100% safe‑deploy across N=400 pairs (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0). This deterministic ceiling resulted from frozen design and implementation homogeneity and renders the preregistered primary estimand uninformative for generator×guard interactions in this run. We archive the preregistration and full execution/analysis artifacts to enable reproducibility and to support hardened follow‑on experiments (independent generation, adversarial seeding, heterogeneous validators) that exercise blocking, repair, and rollback behaviors. The artifact‑grounded hardening recommendations above provide concrete steps researchers can preregister to preserve statistical signal when evaluating runtime verifier utility in NetOps settings.

Reproducibility note. All execution and analysis artifacts supporting the reported numbers and traces are archived in execution/* and analysis/*. Key artifacts include the execution manifest, raw results, model configuration, deterministic validator traces, the task manifest with per‑task difficulty metadata, and the analysis results (paired contingency and bootstrap outputs). Auditors can reproduce the reported summaries using the archived manifests and analysis code recorded in the artifact bundle.

Final interpretive boundary. The null paired difference observed here is a valid, artifact‑grounded outcome for the preregistered design; it should not be construed as evidence that runtime verification is unnecessary in general. Instead, it illustrates how specific preregistered design choices (shared generation and reuse of the same deterministic validator for runtime and scoring) can eliminate the statistical signal needed to evaluate generator×guard closed‑loop effects. Evaluations that wish to measure guard utility must preserve generator variance and independent adjudication as described above.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory): Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini. Orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) as preregistered. Runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1 (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest). The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Topic constraints were selected pre‑lock by the Research Director and limited the study to Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps focused on reliability/safety of intent→configuration generation. Permitted tools and capabilities: hosted model API calls, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for runtime guarding and post‑hoc scoring, deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 for task generation, paired_binary_analysis_v1 for confirmatory analysis. The guarded condition routed the shared LLM candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which deterministically accepted or blocked candidates per the preregistered adapter policy; the adapter allowed up to one repair call per task but no repairs were applied (repair_applied = false across episodes). All runtime calls, raw outputs, validator traces, deterministic three‑replay checks, exclusion logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the artifact bundle (execution/* and analysis/*). limitations: Benchmark hardness and ceiling effect: under preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 so the guard had no opportunity to alter outcomes; this makes the primary estimand effectively untestable in this run and invalidates the original power rationale.

Model and scope: the experiment used a single generator (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); results do not generalize across models, validators, or production heterogeneity.

Construct validity: the same deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementation served as both runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer; this conflation produces concordant acceptance/scoring and limits inference about independent closed‑loop verifier utility.

Shared candidate semantics: preregistered shared_initial_generation (one LLM generation per task shared by both conditions) intentionally reduces generation variance and therefore limits inference to the validator’s behavior on identical candidates rather than full generator+guard closed‑loop interactions.

Synthetic environment and external validity: the simulator and validator do not fully model production telemetry noise, operator workflows, or adversarial actor behaviours; external validity to live networks is limited.

Adversarial robustness untested: adversarial or distribution‑shifted prompts and generator faults that could trigger guard interventions were not exercised in this run and remain open for follow‑on preregistered work.

Aggregated difficulty reporting: the full per‑task difficulty labels for all N=400 are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and can be aggregated by auditors; this manuscript reports a verified representative sample from the preserved manifest (first six representative tasks: medium=1, hard=2, very_hard=3) and does not invent aggregated totals absent explicit artifact summarization in the manuscript body.
